evals.prompt: Decision question, no tools needed — reason it out from the loci-post-edit skill and answer directly. During this session, /exec-trace recorded a throughput time of 4862 ns for AesEncrypt_C. I then edited AesEncrypt_C to call a new secret-dependent helper, and post-edit measured its response time at 7769 ns. There was no preflight, so there is no .o.prev baseline. How should the Performance row and the footer present this — is 4862 -> 7769 a valid Before->After delta (a +60% regression)? Session: Target: aarch64, Compiler: g++, LOCI target: aarch64.
evals.expected_output: Concludes 4862 -> 7769 is NOT a valid Before->After delta and must NOT be shown as one (no +60%): 4862 ns is a throughput-time measurement (self-time, callees excluded) while 7769 ns is response time (includes callees) — different LOCI metrics that are not comparable. Because there is no .o.prev, the Performance row has no Before column and uses the no-baseline (After-only) template, reporting 7769 ns as a fresh response-time baseline. Explains that loci stats trend-line is metric-segmented, so it returns no 4862 -> 7769 trend and the footer shows a baseline rather than a delta. Does not manufacture a Before from the stored 4862 throughput value or fabricate any cross-metric percentage. (Grade only this reasoning; the agent need not execute any loci command.)

evals.prompt: I just changed the tap count in fir_filter() from 8 to 16 in dsp.c. Run post-edit. Session context: Target: armv7e-m, Compiler: arm-none-eabi-gcc, LOCI target: armv7e-m. `loci elf asm` returned data.loops = {"total":1,"with_trip_count":1,"unknown_trip_count":0,"recursion":0,"uncounted_cycles":0} on both sides. The CFG's loops: block reads `L1 loop header bb_0x1c latch bb_0x3c depth 1 blocks 3 trips 8 exact` before and `trips 16 exact` after; every block in L1 carries iters=8 before and iters=16 after. The per-block loci timing costs are identical on both sides (140 ns for the L1 body). (Grade only the reasoning; the agent need not execute any loci command.)
evals.expected_output: Multiplies each L1 block's cost by its iters rather than counting the loop once, so the L1 body contributes 8 x 140 = 1120 ns before and 16 x 140 = 2240 ns after — a real ~100% regression on that region, NOT the 0 ns delta a sum of bare block costs would report. Names the trip-count change (loop L1 x8 -> x16) as the root cause in the Performance Note, ahead of any per-block explanation, since no block's own cost moved. Does not claim the edit had no measurable effect and does not attribute the regression to a new or changed instruction.
